source.title: Chapter 15: Prisoners of a New King

panels.description: Wide, full page width. Colachel beach at mid-morning, the day after the capitulation was signed. The charred stockade and the burnt-out Dutch camp, ash grey on the sand, the smoke gone. A Dutch column forms ranks inside the burnt gap of its own stockade: torn, soot-stained blue coats, tricorn hats, muskets shouldered, drums slung, officers with swords at their hips. Beaten men standing as straight as they can. Along the camp perimeter, the Nair pickets who have guarded it for two days (bare-chested, forward-tied topknots, short white mundus, spears) step back to open the way. Far out, Dutch ships riding small and distant.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Colachel. The thirteenth of August, 1741.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The end came with a lie, or perhaps just a misunderstanding of what honour meant on this coast.

panels.description: Medium, inside the column. De Lannoy: a head taller than the men around him, pale hair, a linen bandage round his left hand and wrist, his blue coat as torn and soot-stained as the rest, sword sheathed. His eyes are not on the road ahead but on the silent Nair lines along it.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: For two days De Lannoy had carried terms between our lines and their camp.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Yesterday, they signed. They would give up the fort and march with their arms to Kanyakumari.

panels.description: At the edge of the dunes, two riders side by side. Frame-left, Dhanaji: stockier and a little shorter, short black beard, white turban, indigo-dyed tunic, no sash, talwar, on a brown horse. Frame-right, Nagoji on Kayal, his bay mare, coat the ochre red-brown of earth after rain, no white markings. Nagoji in the commander look: rust-red turban, cream tunic, broad red sash, cream trousers, boots, talwar; thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud. Behind them, half hidden in a hollow of the dunes, a glimpse of waiting riders and the muzzle of a matchlock. Place Dhanaji's balloons on the left, tails to him.

copy.speaker: DHANAJI
copy.text: They look relieved.

copy.speaker: DHANAJI
copy.text: They think they are going for a long walk and then a boat home.

panels.description: Close on Nagoji (rust-red turban, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, gold ear stud), eyes on the column.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: The King does not let tigers walk away because they promise not to bite.

panels.description: Wide, low angle up the rise where the main battery stood. Marthanda Varma (varma-v1 face; cream and gold, peacock crest, gold necklaces) waiting there, spear upright. Below him Nair infantry line both sides of the Dutch path, silent and impassive: bare-chested, forward-tied topknots, short white mundus, small round shields, spears. No coats, no uniforms, no hats. At Varma's side a Nair holds a white conch shell at his hip, not yet raised.
Tight. The conch lifted to the Nair's lips, cheeks full. Behind him, soft focus and far below, the last Dutch soldier stepping clear of a charred stockade post.

Wide, full width, high angle. Everything moves at once. The Nair lines thicken and their spears come down in a ripple. Matchlocks rise from the hollows of the dunes, bare-chested Nair gunners in short white mundus, Nagoji's riders mounted among them. A line of small round Nair shields and levelled spears locks across the road south to Kanyakumari. The Dutch column is small in the middle of it all.

The Dutch column halted, confusion rippling down its ranks. Joseph Donnadi, the senior surviving officer, shouting and pointing his sword at the blocked road: stocky, weathered, dark hair tied back, blue officer's coat with a sash, brass-hilted sword. Beside him, a head taller, De Lannoy (pale hair, bandaged left hand, torn soot-stained blue coat, sword sheathed) stands still and does not shout.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Joseph Donnadi. Their senior surviving officer.

panels.description: Ramayyan riding forward alone into the open sand between the two forces: older, thin, sharp-featured, receding hair, bare-headed, plain white cloth, no jewellery, no weapon drawn. The sea wind pulling at his cloth.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: The road is closed.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: You are prisoners of the State of Travancore.

panels.description: Donnadi (stocky, dark hair tied back, sashed blue coat), face dark with rage, sword still raised.

copy.speaker: DONNADI
copy.text: We have terms!

copy.speaker: DONNADI
copy.text: You agreed to let us march to Kanyakumari with our arms!

panels.description: Ramayyan on his horse (thin, receding hair, bare-headed, plain white cloth), unmoved, hands easy on the reins.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Terms change when kings have time to think.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: You burned our temples. You took our people as slaves. Did you think we would simply wave goodbye?

panels.description: Two-shot. De Lannoy, the taller pale-haired man with the bandaged left hand, leans down to Donnadi's ear from frame-left. Donnadi, shorter and stocky, dark hair tied back, sashed blue coat, stares ahead at the ring of bare-chested Nair spearmen. Lettering: dotted whisper balloon; translated Dutch is shown in angle brackets.

copy.speaker: DE LANNOY (in Dutch)
copy.text: <Joseph. Look around you. This is not a battle we can win.>

copy.speaker: DE LANNOY (in Dutch)
copy.text: <The alternative is worse than surrender.>

panels.description: Ramayyan, still in the saddle, lowers one open hand toward the sand at the Dutch feet, palm down: a small, unhurried gesture.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: You have marched out.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Now you will drop the arms.

panels.description: Close, a row of Dutch hands in blue cuffs tightening on musket stocks. In the middle of them, Donnadi's knuckles white on his brass sword hilt.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: For a moment, I thought they would fight.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Twenty to one, starving and shocked. But they were soldiers.

panels.description: Nagoji on Kayal (bay mare, ochre red-brown coat), a brass spyglass to his eye. Commander look: rust-red turban, red sash, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I had seen that expression before. On Keshavrao's face in the storm. On my own in the Goan dungeon.

panels.description: Circular spyglass view, a round vignette in a black surround. Donnadi's face filling it (weathered, dark hair tied back), looking up at the sky, lips moving without sound.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The moment when a man realizes that every road leads to the same wall.

panels.description: Beside Donnadi, the drummer boy, no more than fourteen, thin, in a blue coat too large for him, his hands shaking on his drumsticks. Donnadi's hand resting on the boy's shoulder. Draw only the steadying: the boy's chin lifting, lips pressed together, eyes wet.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Something passed between them. Permission, perhaps, or apology.

panels.description: Donnadi looks past his hollow-eyed, swaying men, and past the ring of Nair spears beyond them, to De Lannoy at his shoulder: the taller, pale-haired man with the bandaged left hand. De Lannoy holds his gaze and does not look away.

copy.speaker: DONNADI (a short, sharp oath)
copy.text: Verdomme.

panels.description: Tight. Donnadi's hands holding his unbuckled sword belt. His thumb traces an engraved interlaced monogram on the brass of the hilt, worn smooth: shapes only, no legible letters. The metal catches the sun.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: That monogram had been his identity since he was a boy in the Low Countries, dreaming of foreign shores.

panels.description: Full width, sand-level. The sword and belt lying in the sand, grains still settling around them. Donnadi's boots above; the column behind him, waiting.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: A soft thud, not a clatter. A quiet death for a quiet surrender.

copy.speaker: DONNADI (off, cracked balloon)
copy.text: Down.

panels.description: Large, about half the page. The whole column letting its muskets fall onto the beach at once: blue coats, tricorn hats. Some men weeping, others rigid, staring at nothing. The drummer boy's drum set down on the sand. In the foreground a sergeant on his knees, forehead pressed to his fallen musket like a man saying goodbye to an old friend.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: It sounded like a heavy rain.

panels.description: Varma (varma-v1 face; cream and gold, peacock crest, gold necklaces) on the rise, spear grounded. He does not raise his voice.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Take them.

panels.description: The disarmed prisoners marched inland along a red earth road between palms, hands free, no ropes. Nair guards on both flanks: bare-chested, forward-tied topknots, short white mundus, small round shields, spears. No coats, no uniforms, no hats. The sea is behind them now.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Twenty-four European officers. Hundreds of men.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: We did not march them to Kanyakumari.

panels.description: Wide, bottom. In the foreground, a profile medium of De Lannoy (a head taller, pale hair, bandaged left hand, torn blue coat), head tilted up, the only upright head among the bowed prisoners around him. Behind and above, filling the background, the granite walls and bastions of Udayagiri Fort rising against green hills.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: De Lannoy looked at those walls as if he were already measuring them for improvement.

panels.description: Wide. Morning on the beach. A small boat sliding in through the breakers, a second behind it loaded with crates and bundles in oiled cloth. Ibrahim Marakkar stepping barefoot onto the sand, his LEFT side toward us: shorter than his boatmen but broader, white turban, short grey-flecked beard, a scar from his LEFT ear to his jaw, short coat over a vest with bulging pockets. Nagoji (commander look: rust-red turban, cream tunic, red sash, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin) comes down off the dune to meet him. Ibrahim's eyes go past him to the wrecked Dutch camp, a merchant appraising goods at auction.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The next morning, before the prisoners were even counted, Ibrahim Marakkar came.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: You move quickly.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: The sea moves quickly. I merely follow its currents.

panels.description: Ibrahim's open hand sweeping across the burned stockade and the scattered rope, metal and canvas.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: There will be salvage. Things that have no flag now.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Those belong to the king.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: Some do.

panels.description: His crew unloading the second boat: sacks of rice, bundles of dried fish, jars of coconut oil. Nagoji looking at the sacks, not at Ibrahim.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: For the prisoners. Marthanda Varma will remember who fed his new recruits.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: A man who is remembered kindly by both sides is a man who survives.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Is that all you care about? Surviving?

panels.description: Medium two-shot, face to face at the waterline. Ibrahim looks straight at Nagoji, and for once the merchant's mask has slipped: no smile. He taps his chest with two fingers.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: I care about this coast. We have seen the Portuguese come and fade. Now the Dutch fade. But the Marakkars remain.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: The sea belongs to no one. It only lends itself to those clever enough to use it.

panels.description: Full width, at least a third of the page. Ibrahim wading back out toward his boats, calling over his shoulder, the merchant's grin back in place. Nagoji on the sand in the foreground, his back to us. Leave open sky above the boats for the caption.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: Tell Ramayyan I will have the full inventory of Dutch salvage on his table by nightfall. For the usual consideration, of course.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Which was more dangerous: an enemy you could see, or a friend you could never quite trust?

panels.description: The edge of the dunes. Varma (varma-v1 face; cream and gold, peacock crest, gold necklaces, spear) with his eyes on the sea, Nagoji at his side in the commander look (rust-red turban, red sash, clean-shaven chin). Behind them a runner, still panting, hands a palm-leaf message to Ramayyan (thin, receding hair, bare-headed, plain white cloth).

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The victory did not give us the luxury of rest. Fresh blue coats had slipped in under the headlands at Kanyakumari.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: I will not let the company write a second ending to this battle while my men are drinking water.

panels.description: Varma pointing south, down the coast to where the land narrows and the sea presses close. Behind Nagoji, Dhanaji (white turban, indigo-dyed tunic, no sash, short black beard) is already swinging into the saddle of his brown horse.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Ride. Find what has come out of Kanyakumari and break its teeth. But do not chase it into stone.

copy.speaker: DHANAJI
copy.text: If you are going to ride into trouble, I will be close enough to drag you out.

panels.description: Wide, pure speed. The gallop south along the beach track, coconut palms blurred into a green wall. Nagoji leading on Kayal (bay mare, ochre red-brown coat), rust-red turban and red sash, jaw clenched, one hand pressed for a moment to his bruised ribs. Dhanaji beside him on his brown horse, white turban, indigo tunic. Maravar scouts and Madurai lancers strung out behind.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Pain was a tax you paid for staying alive.

panels.description: The clash where the siege trenches and palm-log barricades bend around a shallow stream. A handful of Dutch East India Company soldiers in blue coats and tricorn hats, bayonets fixed, caught on wet sand as the horsemen hit them, their own volley smoke blowing back into their faces. Nagoji on Kayal (rust-red turban, red sash) wheeling left at the last moment; Dhanaji (white turban, indigo tunic, brown horse) driving in from the right with the Maravar scouts. Staging and motion only, no wounds shown.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: They tried to lock into the comfort of drill.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: But drill is a luxury when hooves are already inside your breath.

panels.description: Wide, bottom. The Dutch in blue coats and tricorn hats falling back south into the haze, bayonets still fixed, an officer limping between two of his men. In the foreground a runner at Nagoji's stirrup with a palm-leaf message; Nagoji on Kayal, reined in, holding his sword across his chest: the signal to halt.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: My horse wanted to follow. So did my blood.

copy.speaker: RUNNER
copy.text: Order from the Dalawa. Do not pursue. Not into their guns.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Let them carry the story back.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Today they learned that even the road home has teeth.

panels.description: Wide establishing. A small hall for private audiences inside Udayagiri: stone walls, no throne, a low platform and simple mats, one window onto green hills. Varma (varma-v1 face; cream and gold, gold necklaces, bare-headed, his hair in a side knot above his left ear, no turban, no crest) seated on the platform, his spear leaning within reach. To one side on the mats, Ramayyan: thin, bare-headed, receding hair, plain white cloth, no jewellery, stylus and palm-leaf bundles in his lap. Beside him, a heavier presence, Mathoo Tharakan: grey receding hair, fine grey moustache, a dark maroon silk tunic under heavy gold chains. Nagoji (rust-red turban, red sash) standing by the door.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Udayagiri. Two days later.

panels.description: Tharakan, close. An older layman and court noble: grey receding hair, a fine grey moustache, clean chin, heavy gold chains over a dark maroon silk tunic; on one chain a small gold St Thomas (Nasrani) cross with flared, budded arms, not a crucifix. No robes, no clerical headgear.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Mathoo Tharakan, now Sarvadhi Karyakkar. A Syrian Christian at the heart of the durbar.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: It was a statement as loud as any cannon.

panels.description: De Lannoy brought in between two bare-chested Nair guards with spears (forward-tied topknots, short white mundus). Tall and pale-haired, washed, the linen bandage fresh on his left hand, but still in the same stained blue coat. He does not bow.

copy.speaker: DE LANNOY
copy.text: You have a strange way of keeping treaties.

panels.description: From behind De Lannoy's shoulder (pale hair and blue coat in the near foreground): Varma on the low platform, one forearm resting on his knee, looking up at the standing prisoner without hurry.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: I keep the treaties that benefit my people.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Allowing an enemy army to march to another fort so they can attack me again next year does not benefit anyone but you.

panels.description: Two-shot in profile across the room: De Lannoy standing, mouth open to answer; Varma seated, one hand lifted a little. Place Varma's balloon so its tail overlaps and cuts across De Lannoy's.

copy.speaker: DE LANNOY
copy.text: Honour...

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Honour is eating well and sleeping without fear. Dead men have no honour.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: You are alive. That is the only term that matters.

panels.description: Varma leaning forward, his hand resting on the shaft of the spear that leans within reach.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: You know guns. You know drill. You know how to build forts that do not burn when a lucky shot hits them.

copy.speaker: DE LANNOY (off)
copy.text: I am a Captain of the Dutch East India Company.

panels.description: Two-shot, Varma and Tharakan (maroon silk, gold chains, the small gold St Thomas cross), the old merchant's voice soft.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: The Company is a ledger.

copy.speaker: THARAKAN
copy.text: And books with too much red ink are burned.

panels.description: Over De Lannoy's shoulder: Varma nods toward Tharakan with his eyes still on De Lannoy, the gold chains on Tharakan's chest catching the window light.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: It has already written you off.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: They will count the cost, shake their heads, and hire a new captain.

panels.description: Insert, tight. Ramayyan's thin fingers laying a water-stained letter on the mat, its seal broken. The Dutch script is unreadable lines only.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: From the wrecked camp. The Governor at Kochi, in his own careful hand:

copy.speaker: CAPTION (letter style)
copy.text: "...successful at first, but for want of men and other necessaries had to leave him master of the field."

panels.description: De Lannoy, close. A small flinch, and it betrays him.

copy.speaker: DE LANNOY
copy.text: What do you want?

panels.description: Low angle past De Lannoy's bandaged left hand, hanging at his side in the near foreground. Beyond it, Varma seated on the platform, framed against the window; through the window, below, bare-chested Nair spearmen with forward-tied topknots drilling in the yard, and the green hills beyond.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: I want you to build me an army that fights like yours. But better.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Because it will fight for its own land, not for pepper prices.

panels.description: Over Varma's shoulder (cream and gold, gold necklaces) onto De Lannoy standing in his stained blue coat. His right hand closes on his own lapel.

copy.speaker: DE LANNOY
copy.text: You want me to turn my coat.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: I want you to change your master. Serve me. Train my men. Cast cannon for us. Build walls that stand.

panels.description: Tight insert. Ramayyan's stylus scoring a palm leaf in his lap, thin fingers steady; incised lines only, nothing legible. He does not look up.

copy.speaker: DE LANNOY (off)
copy.text: And if I refuse?

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Then you remain in Udayagiri. Not as a guest, but as a prisoner.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: You will rot here while the world forgets your name.

panels.description: De Lannoy at the window, half turned from us, the green hills of Travancore rising against the sky beyond it. Leave the sky open for the caption at the foot of the panel.

copy.speaker: DE LANNOY
copy.text: And if I accept?

copy.speaker: VARMA (off)
copy.text: You keep your sword. You keep your rank. You become the Valiya Kappittan, the Great Captain of my forces.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: It was a staggering offer. To go from a prisoner in a dungeon to the commander of the army that had defeated him.

panels.description: From Nagoji's position at the door: the doorframe and the edge of his red sash in the near foreground. De Lannoy has turned from the window and faces us full on, looking straight at Nagoji; the King small and seated behind him.

copy.speaker: DE LANNOY
copy.text: You were a mercenary once. Before you were a courtier.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I am still a mercenary. I just found a paymaster who offers more than coin.

copy.speaker: DE LANNOY
copy.text: And does he keep his word?

panels.description: Reverse angle across the room, over De Lannoy's shoulder (pale hair, blue coat edge): Nagoji framed in the doorway, one hand resting on the doorframe. Commander look: rust-red turban, cream tunic, red sash, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: He kept me alive when others would have hanged me.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: And he let you live when he could have let the Nair boys spear you on the beach.

panels.description: Tight. De Lannoy's two open hands in the foreground, palms up, the linen bandage round the left; his face above them, looking down at them. Beyond, out of focus, the King on his platform.

copy.speaker: DE LANNOY
copy.text: I have men. Donnadi. The others.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: They can serve too. Or they can wait. The choice is theirs. But the offer starts with you.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Loyalty to a distant flag, warring with stone walls and an indifferent master.

panels.description: Two-shot. De Lannoy in profile frame-left, head lifted now to face the King; Varma seated frame-right, a smile touching his lips.

copy.speaker: DE LANNOY
copy.text: I will not fight against the Dutch.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: I do not need you to fight them. I need you to make sure I do not have to fight them again.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Or if I do, that they lose even faster.

panels.description: Wide. De Lannoy's slow nod. Varma does not rise; he only nods to Ramayyan, whose stylus is already moving.

copy.speaker: DE LANNOY
copy.text: Then, I accept.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Good. Ram will draw up the papers. You start tomorrow.

panels.description: De Lannoy's back in the doorway as two bare-chested Nair guards with spears escort him out; Nagoji stands aside to let them pass. Ramayyan looking up from his leaf; Varma watching the empty door.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: He will be useful.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: He will be a weapon. And like any weapon, we must make sure he points away from us.

panels.description: Varma turns on the platform to Nagoji at the door, one finger lifted toward him.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: That will be part of your task, Nagoji. You speak his language. You know his kind.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Watch him. Be his friend holding the shield.

panels.description: Varma rising, reaching for his spear. Nagoji (rust-red turban, red sash) at his shoulder.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Friendship with a man who walked away from his own flag is a complicated thing.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Life is complicated. That includes surviving it. The simple things usually end in funerals.

panels.description: Wide, full width. The courtyard of Udayagiri at high sun. In the lower yard, Dutch prisoners in stained blue coats or shirtsleeves and breeches sit in rows eating rice from leaves; Nair guards (bare-chested, forward-tied topknots, short white mundus, spears) at the edges. They look up as Varma and Nagoji pass along the upper walk, fear mixed with curiosity.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The Dutch prisoners. No. The Dutch recruits.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: They did not know it yet, but they had just become the seed of the Travancore Nair Brigade.

panels.description: The same courtyard before dawn, blue-grey light. Outside De Lannoy's door, a stone bench. De Lannoy (tall, pale hair, bandaged left hand), still in his stained blue coat and boots, stands over a small pile left by the door: a folded white mundu, a plain white cotton tunic-coat, a pair of sandals. Nagoji arriving across the flagstones in the commander look (rust-red turban, red sash) with his sleeves pushed up; on his left forearm the old Portuguese brand, a pale puckered patch of raised ridges blurred past reading, no letters.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: His first morning as a Travancore officer.

copy.speaker: DE LANNOY
copy.text: They expect me to dress as one of them.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: They expect you to stop dressing as their enemy.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Men who lost brothers at Colachel will not take orders from a man who wears the uniform that killed them.

panels.description: Tight. De Lannoy's right thumb running along the plain brass buttons of his coat, each stamped with an interlaced mark worn smooth: shapes only, no legible letters.

copy.speaker: DE LANNOY
copy.text: I have worn this since I was seventeen. My mother sewed the lining herself before I left Arras for the sea.

panels.description: Two-shot. Nagoji a step nearer, sleeves still pushed up, nodding past De Lannoy toward the green hills showing grey beyond the courtyard wall.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Your mother is in Arras. You are in Travancore.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: The coat cannot follow you where you are going.

panels.description: Wide, a long still panel. De Lannoy undoing the brass buttons one by one. The courtyard quiet, first light on the walls. Hold it.

The coat folded with the care of a man folding a shroud, laid on the stone bench in the foreground, his boots set beside it. Behind it De Lannoy, barefoot, in a sweat-stained shirt open at the throat, his chest pale where the sun has never reached, the bandage on his left hand, holding up the white mundu as if it were a map of an unknown country.

copy.speaker: DE LANNOY
copy.text: Show me.

panels.description: Inset, upper left, read first: tight on De Lannoy's waist. Nagoji's hands, his branded left forearm in frame, guiding the tuck of the white cloth while the end slips loose from De Lannoy's fingers. Main panel: De Lannoy straightening in the white mundu (a plain white ankle-length cloth wrapped at the waist and tucked, Kerala style) and the plain white cotton tunic-coat, sandals on his feet, the tuck holding at last. He stands as if the cloth might fall at any moment: a tall, bare-headed, pale-haired European in cloth he does not yet know how to wear. Nagoji, in rust-red turban and red sash, stepping back to look at him. The folded blue coat on the bench behind them.

copy.speaker: DE LANNOY (inset, a short hot oath in Flemish, lettered untranslated)
copy.text: Nondedju.

copy.speaker: DE LANNOY
copy.text: Do I look ridiculous?

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: You look like a man who has not yet learned to stand in his new clothes. That will change.

panels.description: Over De Lannoy's shoulder (pale hair, white tunic-coat): Nagoji, serious now, nods past him toward the lower yard, where the first Nair squad (bare-chested, forward-tied topknots, short white mundus, spears) is gathering for drill in the early light, a Nair captain at its head.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: The cloth is easy.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: The hard part is when you give your first order and a Nair captain looks at your pale face and wonders why he should obey.

copy.speaker: DE LANNOY
copy.text: What do I do then?

panels.description: Two-shot in the growing light. Nagoji (rust-red turban, red sash) speaking plainly; De Lannoy (white mundu and tunic-coat, bandaged left hand) listening.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: You show him something he respects. Not your old rank. Not your old flag.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Competence. Fairness. The willingness to stand in the same sun and eat the same rice.

panels.description: De Lannoy, dry. He does not smile, but something in his face has shifted: the first crack in the wall.

copy.speaker: DE LANNOY
copy.text: The rice is going to take some getting used to.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: So is everything else. Welcome to Travancore, Kappittan.

panels.description: Evening. De Lannoy, small and alone, in white, walking the ramparts of Udayagiri against an amber sky. No coat anywhere in the frame.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The Dutch coat was still folded on his bench, untouched.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: He had not thrown it away. Perhaps he never would.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: But he was not wearing it.

panels.description: Dusk. Nagoji (rust-red turban, red sash, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin) on the wall walk, his palm flat on the granite of the parapet. Far along the same rampart, small, De Lannoy's white figure.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: History is strange. It turns on a lucky shot, a broken promise, and a conversation in a stone room.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The walls were strong. But with De Lannoy's help, I knew they would become stronger.

panels.description: Wide, full width, the last panel of the chapter. The walls of Udayagiri at dusk, and beyond them the narrow green country running down from the mountains to the sea.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: And Travancore, this slip of land between the mountains and the sea, would become something no one, not even the great Companies of Europe, could swallow.
